robinsons-arch.context: A surviving spring of an arch in the western wall of the Temple Mount, identified by Edward Robinson in 1838.

sources.label: Robinson's Arch - Encyclopedia of the Bible

sinaiticus.context: Tischendorf examined leaves in 1844 and a larger portion in 1859. The manuscript was preserved at St Catherine's Monastery; its removal and ownership history remain disputed.

site.label: Letters study
site.note: The discussion of Hebrews' position in the canon names Sinaiticus and cites Westcott's History of the Canon, p. 377. This is a discussion of the manuscript, not a claim that Tischendorf's edition supplies our Bible text.
site.sourceTitle: Westcott, History of the Canon (7th ed., 1896), p. 377

asia-minor.role: Surveyed the region and studied Paul's journeys
asia-minor.context: Ramsay's travel and historical research across Asia Minor began in 1880. This entry represents years of research, not a single discovery. Pisidian Antioch is a representative map location.

sources.label: Ramsay - St. Paul the Traveller and the Roman Citizen (1895)

site.label: Paul's letters
site.note: The Letters study cites Ramsay's 1895 book for chronology and the churches of Galatia. The link is to that named work, not proof of every archaeological interpretation associated with Ramsay.
site.sourceTitle: Ramsay, St. Paul the Traveller and the Roman Citizen (1895), Chronological Index and chapter 5

dead-sea-scrolls.role: Later scholar of the scrolls; not the original finder
dead-sea-scrolls.context: Bedouin shepherds found the first Qumran scrolls in 1947. Yigael Yadin later studied the scrolls; the discovery should not be credited to him.

sources.label: Israel Museum - Digital Dead Sea Scrolls
Israel Museum - Yigael Yadin and the scrolls

jericho.context: Kathleen Kenyon's team excavated Jericho from 1952 to 1958, refining its archaeological sequence from the Neolithic to the Late Bronze Age. This dates a campaign, not the first discovery of the city.

sources.label: Council for British Research in the Levant - Excavations at Jericho

hazor.role: Led the Hebrew University excavation team
hazor.context: Yigael Yadin led excavations at Hazor in the 1950s and 1960s, including the 1955-1958 campaign. Later teams continued work at the site.

sources.label: Hebrew University - excavation history and faculty

masada.context: Yigael Yadin directed the major excavation campaign at Masada from 1963 to 1965. The dates identify that campaign, not the first recognition of the site.

sources.label: Israel Nature and Parks Authority - History of Masada
